prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: acceptance/transfer→screening/sortation/make-up→Outbound Load Control Desk; airline loading excluded. No explicit modes.
Elements/items: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit stages accepted bags preserving flight; sends Oversize Exception Ticket→Image Resolution Desk (confirms authorized oversize position). Bag Tag Printer produces tags/Calibration Witness Tag; replacements require authorized identity confirmation. Flight Data Gateway (Lantern) maintains flight identity/timing; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory→Baggage Control System (Velvet). Velvet validates eligibility/routes/capacity; records screening/release against flight. Transfer Bag Feeder meters checked transfers; sends Late Transfer Bag Card→Bag Reconciliation Station (reconciles intended flight; sends Bag Match Query). Concourse Zone Controller (Mosslight) assigns active lanes using zone status; produces Recovery Route Card. Induction Tray Conveyor meters safely, avoiding accumulation. North Gate Scanner (Kestrel)/South Gate Scanner verify readable identity; South produces Manual Rescan Receipt. Primary Crossbelt Sorter (Juniper) separates authorized destinations/status; sends Chute Occupancy Note. Secondary Inspection Chute retains unresolved bags pending disposition. East Make-Up Conveyor/West Make-Up Conveyor deliver assigned bags at controlled rates. Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (Orchard) maintains build order/positions; receives Carousel Release Slip after position/flight checks. Airline Ramp Coordinator sends authorized slip; confirms staffing/equipment/loading sequence before acceptance. Outbound Load Control Desk reconciles build/permitted load before closeout. Explosives Response Team (Pebble) manages holds; produces Custody Seal Log. Baggage Operations Supervisor (Tern) coordinates Security Duty Manager, Maintenance Technician, airport security personnel and airline ground operations; authorizes in-window release, reprioritizes, communicates constraints. Security Duty Manager resolves security holds; Maintenance Technician reports restrictions.
Requirements: authorized-only access; unsafe/jammed feeds stop; blocked chutes prohibit release. Incomplete/alarmed screening blocks induction/make-up; threats suspend routing pending authorization. Preserve recoverable bag-flight association. Recovery requires location/identity/outcome/authorization agreement. Compare cutoff windows/allowances with route estimates; earlier departures require review; insufficient/missed windows require deferral/hold/reassignment/recovery. Allocation/release require active flight/position, clearance/capacity. Manual resolution starts when image/identity exceptions prevent reliable automatic disposition.

New part:
S156: Image Resolution Desk presents the available bag image and exception details to the operator for review.
S157: The operator compares visible bag features with the recorded tag number and the handling data associated with the bag.
S158: The operator confirms that the image is legible enough to support a decision and does not rely on an uncertain visual match.
S159: Image Resolution Desk uses the rescan receipt to confirm that a second image was captured under the approved procedure.
S160: When the image remains inconclusive, the operator requests a physical inspection through the established inspection process.
S161: The identity check verifies that the physical tag is attached to the inspected bag and that its number agrees with the recorded bag identity.
S162: Baggage Control System checks the recorded bag identity against the current routing data before any disposition is committed.
S163: Flight Data Gateway provides the flight data used to validate the bag's assigned destination and service date.
S164: Bag Reconciliation Station records whether the inspected bag matches the expected flight assignment.
S165: A mismatch places the bag on hold until an authorized operator resolves the discrepancy or escalates it.
S166: Juniper holds the affected bag from automatic sorting while the manual disposition remains unresolved.
S167: Kestrel captures a readable tag image when the bag is presented for a permitted scan.
S168: North Gate Scanner records the tag read and image data needed to support an operator's identity check.
S169: Secondary Inspection Chute provides a controlled location for bags requiring physical examination.
S170: Explosives Response Team conducts any security examination assigned under applicable procedures.
S171: Baggage Operations Supervisor approves the operational disposition when the case exceeds the operator's authority.
S172: After the identity and flight checks pass, Baggage Control System authorizes the bag to rejoin its previously assigned screening and sort path.
S173: Outbound Load Control Desk confirms that the bag remains eligible for inclusion in the planned flight load.
S174: Airline Ramp Coordinator confirms any flight-side constraint that could prevent the reconciled bag from being accepted.
S175: Concourse Zone Controller applies the authorized routing state without bypassing required screening controls.
S176: Maintenance Technician uses the witness tag to verify that the applicable calibration status was witnessed before equipment returns to service.
S177: If a route or flight assignment has changed, the operator obtains approval before the bag is released into the revised process.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
